newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: TENNIS-FERREIRA GIVES SOUTH AFRICA 2-0 LEAD.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-FERREIRA GIVES SOUTH AFRICA 2-0 LEAD.

text.p: World number eight Wayne Ferreira carried South Africa to a 2-0 lead over Russia after edging Andrei Cherkasov in a five-set marathon in their Davis Cup World Group first round tie on Saturday.
With on-court temperatures reaching 38 degrees Celsius in overcast but humid conditions, Ferreira triumphed 7-5 6-3 3-6 4-6 8-6 in a fluctuating battle lasting four hours and 20 minutes.

Ferreira, ranked 112 places higher than Cherkasov, clinched the first set 7-5 after breaking the Russian in the first game of the day in a singles match continued from Friday when rain stopped play with the score at 5-5.
Unleashing powerful groundstrokes and advancing to the net whenever possible, the 25-year-old Ferreira raced through the second set 6-3 in only 36 minutes after breaking the Russian twice.
But errors crept into Ferreira's play as he appeared to relax and a steadier Cherkasov took the next two sets with two breaks of serve in each.

"A problem I often have is that, after going two sets up, I can start cruising and just go through the motions," Ferreira said. "That helped him to raise his game...I became lethargic and he became aggressive."
The final set was locked at 6-6 before Ferreira hammered three aces to edge ahead 7-6 and then broke the Russian for the fourth time in the set to clinch victory.

"It was very tough out there...an exhausting match," Cherkasov said. "I had a good opportunity to win after a break in the fifth set and I saw that Wayne was also physically tired. But I just didn't play well enough on a few of the big points and he deserved to win."
Saturday's doubles match between South Africa's Ellis Ferreira and Grant Stafford and Cherkasov and Andrei Olhovsky was postponed until Sunday morning.

"The Russian team captain has exercised his team's right not to call upon a player to play another match on the same day if he has already played 30 games or more earlier," American match referee Ken Farrar said. "This obviously applies, in this case to Andrei Cherkasov."
